reason: The cited evidence does not directly address the HfMoTaTiZr system or the effect of Hf/Zr substitution on density or mechanical properties. E1 discusses general solid-solution strengthening in a different alloy system, E2 shows that Ta and Zr can cause phase separation and embrittlement in HfNbTaTiZr-derived alloys, and E3 only reports lattice parameter and grain size changes with Zr content in unspecified MEAs, without mechanical data. None of the key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: Hf and Zr are chemically similar and have similar atomic sizes, promoting retention of a single-phase BCC structure
Substituting Hf with lower-density Zr will reduce the alloy's overall density
Retention of the single-phase BCC structure and lattice distortion will maintain solid-solution strengthening
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature yield strength near 1600 MPa and 1000 °C yield strength near 855 MPa
The modified alloy will retain comparable ductility to the baseline
